meta.title: The "Unassigned" pseudo-project (null object pattern)
meta.description:
## Design decision

'Unassigned' is a real, permanent project row — not a null/optional projectId anywhere in the model. Every signal gets a projectId the moment Auto-Assign Signal processes it, whether or not a Sender Rule matched.

Properties:
- Always exists; not created via CreateProject, not counted in ProjectSlotsView's 6-slot cap, cannot be deleted or recoloured.
- A completely ordinary value for projectId everywhere — AssignSignalToProject.projectId, Signal Assigned To Project.projectId, SignalsListView.assignedProject, and a Sender Rule's own target project can all legitimately be 'unassigned'.
- No separate 'ignore' concept: to suppress a sender/group, create a normal Sender Rule whose target project is 'unassigned' — the existing contact+group > contact > group specificity resolution handles exceptions for free (e.g. 'everyone in this group goes to Family, except this one person → Unassigned').
- The Signals screen shows every signal, always, filterable by project — 'Unassigned' is just one more filter value, not a separate inbox/backlog state.

Still open: exactly how/when the 'unassigned' project row itself comes into existence (it isn't a business event — more like seed/bootstrap data, similar to how ProjectColourPaletteView and ScheduleOptionsView are static config rather than event-sourced). Treat it the same way: a permanent static row, not something CreateProject ever produces.
